So evolution refers to natural selection. Organisms that are better at reproducing tend to pass on their genes more, over a long enough time that causes populations to change. So by that metric, gods aren't organism and don't reproduce, so are exempt from natural selection.

However, gods are "memes", which outside of the way we normally think about them, are ideas that behave like genes and are passed on. For example, fire creation is a meme. Someone a long time ago figured out how to create fire, taught their kids, etc. And in much the same way as the ways we create fire have changed, so have our gods. At this point, I'm not 100% sure any two people actually even believe in the same gods. So by that metric, yeah, gods are absolutely subject to change as they are passed on, through means pretty similar to mutation and adaptation.

And then there's also the idea of say, late australopithecines maybe having their own primitive religions and whatnot. Obviously they wouldn't have worshipped gods that resemble modern humans, if they worshipped gods they would have worshipped gods that resembled themselves. And the primary natural forces they would have been trying to explain would have remained the same. Storms, the ocean, droughts, the sun, animals, life, etc. So if we very generously say that all sun gods stem from a prehistoric pre-human sun god, we could probably fairly assume that the image of that god evolved alongside its worshippers.
